profile.reading: This is BNY Mellons data center at 636 Pierce Street in Somerset, in Franklin Township, Somerset County, New Jersey, built in 2001 and listed as fully operational in industry directories, connected to the PJM regional electric grid. Neither square footage nor power capacity in megawatts is publicly disclosed for this facility in sources checked this session, including specialized data center market trackers, consistent with the more limited public disclosure typical of large custody banks internal enterprise data centers, which BNY Mellon and peer institutions generally treat as sensitive, undisclosed infrastructure for security reasons. BNY Mellon, formally the Bank of New York Mellon and now branded simply BNY, is a major American custody bank and financial services company providing asset servicing, investment management, and banking services to institutional and corporate clients globally. This registry records the facilitys confirmed address, operational status, and 2001 build year as verified facts, while treating the absence of capacity or size figures as an honest gap rather than an oversight, given that even specialized data center directories were unable to surface those numbers for this facility. Somerset, within Franklin Township, sits in central New Jersey along the Interstate 287 corridor, an area with a long history of hosting corporate back office and data processing operations for major New York City area financial institutions, given its relative proximity to Manhattan combined with lower real estate costs than the city itself, a pattern also seen in the choice of nearby New Jersey sites by other major banks. BNY Mellon traces its own history to the Bank of New York, founded in 1784 by Alexander Hamilton, making it one of the oldest banks in the United States, and the modern BNY Mellon was formed through the 2007 merger of the Bank of New York and Mellon Financial Corporation.

BNY Mellon operates a data center campus in Franklin Township, Somerset County, New Jersey. The operator publishes no power capacity, square footage, or IT load specification for this facility. The research status is complete, confirming that no such figures appear on BNY Mellon's corporate site or other public sources searched.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only five publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 MW. This campus ranks sixth by published megawattage in the state, meaning it either publishes no figure or is among the five published sites. Without a published specification, this campus cannot be ranked against other AI-scale facilities or assessed for its contribution to regional compute capacity.

The absence of published detail makes this facility invisible to the analysis of AI infrastructure scaling.
